mainTopic: The end of the story of משה and ארך אפים, the crown of humble צדיקים, and the משנה and גמרא on עיר הנדחת, including whether a city can be split between two שבטים
overview: The amud opens by finishing the story of משה and ארך אפים: משה reminds הקב״ה that patience is even for רשעים. רבי חגא then learns from two פסוקים in תהלים that what משה saw was ארך אפים. Next, the גמרא teaches that הקב״ה will be a crown for humble צדיקים. It also reads ישעיהו 28:6 as praise for people who control their יצר, judge truthfully, and toil in תורה, while those who stumble in judgment end up in גיהנם. Then a new משנה begins about עיר הנדחת, a city led into idol worship. It lists the conditions for judging the city as a whole, what happens to the people and their property, and the מחלוקת between רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא about the ruined land. The גמרא starts by learning the conditions from the words of the פסוק. It then brings a מחלוקת between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש on whether one city can be split between two שבטים. רבי יוחנן's two proofs are pushed aside, and the challenge to the second answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: משה reminds God: You said slow to anger is even for the wicked
steps.stepSummary: משה answers הקב״ה by reminding Him of His own words: ארך אפים applies even to רשעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: משה said before Him: Master of the World, didn't You tell me that it is 'even for the wicked'?
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of a story that began earlier. After the sin of the מרגלים, הקב״ה reminded משה that he had said ארך אפים is only for צדיקים, and now משה answers back with הקב״ה's own words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, משה asked whether ארך אפים is only for צדיקים, and הקב״ה answered: 'even for the wicked.' Now that ישראל have sinned, משה uses that very answer to ask for patience. He turns הקב״ה's words into his argument for mercy.

keyTerms.meaning: Master of the World, a way of addressing הקב״ה
Slow to anger, patience (the מידה this whole story is about)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this line as משה changing his mind on his own. He is quoting back what הקב״ה told him earlier in the story.

phrases.english: He said before Him:
Master of the World,
didn't You say this to me:
"even for the wicked"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְפָנָיו: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, וְלֹא כָּךְ אָמַרְתָּ לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a dialogue begun before this section, answering הקב״ה's reminder to משה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: משה answers that הקב״ה Himself said ארך אפים applies even to רשעים, so it should apply now.

steps.title: The verse where משה says 'as You have spoken'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that this conversation is hinted in the פסוק 'ועתה יגדל נא כח ה׳ כאשר דברת לאמר.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what is written: 'And now, please let the power of the Lord be great, as You have spoken, saying.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects the story to a real פסוק, where משה prays for ישראל and says 'as You have spoken.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'כאשר דברת' (as You have spoken) hint that משה was quoting something הקב״ה had already told him. According to the story, that 'something' is 'ארך אפים, even for רשעים.' This gives the story a source in the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what is written, a phrase linking a teaching to a פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: משה's prayer after the מרגלים, 'as You have spoken,' points back to הקב״ה's promise that ארך אפים is even for רשעים.

phrases.english: And this is what is written:
"And now, please let the power of the Lord be great,
as You have spoken, saying."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Grounds משה's words in step 1 in a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That משה reminded הקב״ה of His promise of ארך אפים even for רשעים.

steps.title: רבי חגא overhears a child reciting verses
steps.stepSummary: רבי חגא, climbing the stairs of רבה בר שילא's house, hears a child say a פסוק about 'length of days' followed by 'תפלה למשה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חגא was going up the stairs of רבה בר שילא's house. He heard a child saying: 'Your testimonies are very trustworthy; holiness befits Your house, Lord, for length of days,' and right after it, 'A prayer of משה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story to set up a proof. It describes the two פסוקים the child said one after the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'לארך ימים' (for length of days) sounds like ארך אפים, the long patience of הקב״ה. Right after it comes 'תפלה למשה,' a chapter of משה. This closeness will be used in the next step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chagga was going up
the stairs of the house of Rabba bar Sheila.
He heard a certain child who was saying:
"Your testimonies are very trustworthy;
holiness befits Your house,
Lord, for length of days,"
and right after it: "A prayer of Moshe, etc."
phrases.notes: תהלים 90:1. The child said this right after the first פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חַגָּא הֲוָה סָלֵיק וְאָזֵיל בְּדַרְגָּא דְּבֵי רַבָּה בַּר שֵׁילָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts to a new story that will add support to the theme of משה and ארך אפים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A story setting up a proof: 'לארך ימים' was said right before 'תפלה למשה.'

steps.title: רבי חגא concludes משה saw ארך אפים
steps.stepSummary: From the closeness of the פסוקים, רבי חגא concludes that what משה saw was the מידה of ארך אפים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Learn from this that it was 'slow to anger' that משה saw.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חגא draws his conclusion from the two פסוקים he heard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא asked what משה 'saw' that made him bow down, and one opinion said ארך אפים. Since 'length of days' (patience) sits next to 'A prayer of משה,' רבי חגא sees support for the view that משה saw ארך אפים.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this, a phrase for drawing a conclusion

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חגא supports the view that משה saw the מידה of ארך אפים, using the closeness of 'לארך ימים' and 'תפלה למשה.'

phrases.english: He said: Learn from this
that it was "slow to anger" that he saw.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם רָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the פסוקים heard in step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: משה saw the מידה of ארך אפים.

steps.title: God will be a crown on the head of every righteous person
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי חנינא teaches that in the future הקב״ה will be a crown for each צדיק, based on ישעיהו 28:5.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי חנינא: In the future, הקב״ה will be a crown on the head of every single צדיק, as it says: 'On that day the Lord of hosts will be a crown of glory and a diadem of beauty for the remnant of His people.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins about the reward of צדיקים in the future.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source is ישעיהו 28:5, which calls הקב״ה a 'crown' and 'diadem.' The next steps will explain who exactly gets this crown.

keyTerms.meaning: In the future, is destined to

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Chanina:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, is destined to be
a crown on the head of every single righteous person,
as it says:
"On that day the Lord of hosts will be
a crown of glory and a diadem of beauty
for the remnant of His people, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: עָתִיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִהְיוֹת עֲטָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, the future reward of צדיקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הקב״ה will be a crown on the head of every צדיק.

steps.title: What do 'crown of glory' and 'diadem of beauty' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the two phrases in the פסוק refer to.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'a crown of glory and a diadem of beauty' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question to explain the wording of the פסוק. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses two different images, 'עטרת צבי' and 'צפירת תפארה.' The גמרא wants to know who each image is for.

keyTerms.meaning: Glory; also hints at desire or will

phrases.english: What is meant by "a crown of glory and a diadem of beauty"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the פסוק quoted in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is meant by 'עטרת צבי' and 'צפירת תפארה'?

steps.title: For those who do His will and wait for His salvation
steps.stepSummary: The crown is for those who do רצון הקב״ה, and the diadem is for those who wait for His ישועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For those who do His will and who wait for His salvation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase is read through its sound: 'צבי' points to doing His will, and 'צפירת' points to 'מצפים,' waiting. So two kinds of people are crowned: those who act and those who hope.

phrases.english: For those who do His will
and who wait for His salvation.
phrases.notes: Hear the sound play: צבי can mean 'desire,' and צפירת sounds like מצפים, 'waiting.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'עטרת צבי' is for those who do His will; 'צפירת תפארה' is for those who wait for His ישועה.

steps.title: Only for those who make themselves humble
steps.stepSummary: One might think the crown is for everyone who does His will, so the פסוק says 'לשאר עמו': only for one who sees himself as leftovers.
steps.simpleTranslation: Could it be for everyone? The פסוק teaches: 'for the remnant of His people,' meaning for one who makes himself like leftovers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible broad reading and then pushes it away using the end of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea that every doer of מצוות gets the crown is rejected. The word 'שאר' (remnant, what is left over) limits it to someone humble, who treats himself as unimportant like leftover scraps.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think, a word introducing an idea that will be rejected

steps.whatToRemember: The crown of הקב״ה is for צדיקים who do His will and wait for His ישועה, but only if they are humble, seeing themselves like 'leftovers.'

phrases.english: Could it be for everyone?
phrases.notes: Everyone who does His will and waits for His salvation.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "for the remnant of His people" —
for one who makes himself like leftovers.
phrases.notes: He means someone humble, who doesn't act important.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the group described in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the crown is for all who do His will and wait for His ישועה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It ignores the word 'שאר,' which limits the reward to the humble.

steps.title: The next verse in Isaiah is quoted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes ישעיהו 28:6 in order to explain it phrase by phrase.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And for a spirit of justice to the one who sits in judgment, and for strength to those who turn back battle at the gate.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next פסוק. This is a setup: the following steps will explain each part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the simple level the פסוק speaks of judges and soldiers. The גמרא will read each phrase as a picture of spiritual work.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who turn back the battle

phrases.english: "And for a spirit of justice to the one who sits in judgment,
and for strength to those who turn back battle at the gate."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the פסוק right after the one in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Quotes ישעיהו 28:6 for explanation.

steps.title: Ruling over the inclination and judging truthfully
steps.stepSummary: 'רוח משפט' is one who rules over his יצר; 'היושב על המשפט' is one who judges a true judgment truthfully.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And for a spirit of justice': this is one who rules over his inclination. 'To the one who sits in judgment': this is one who judges a true judgment truthfully.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first half of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Justice' is read first as judging oneself, keeping the יצר הרע in check. Then the judge in the פסוק is one whose ruling is fully true, not just technically correct.

keyTerms.meaning: One who rules over his (evil) inclination

phrases.english: "And for a spirit of justice" —
this is one who rules over his inclination,
"to the one who sits in judgment" —
this is one who judges a true judgment truthfully,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first half of the פסוק quoted in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק praises one who controls his יצר and one who judges with complete truth.

steps.title: Strength, the battle of Torah, and the gate of the study hall
steps.stepSummary: 'גבורה' is overcoming the יצר; 'משיבי מלחמה' is arguing in the battle of תורה; 'שערה' is those who come early and stay late in בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And for strength': this is one who overpowers his inclination. 'Those who turn back battle': this is one who debates in the battle of תורה. 'At the gate': these are those who come early and stay late in בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second half of the פסוק, finishing the דרשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Real 'strength' is beating the יצר, as in 'איזהו גבור.' The 'battle' is the back-and-forth of learning תורה, and the 'gate' is the doorway of the shul and בית מדרש, where devoted people arrive first and leave last.

keyTerms.meaning: Gives and takes, debates back and forth in learning
The battle of תורה, the debate of learning

steps.whatToRemember: ישעיהו 28:6 is read as praise for spiritual heroes: those who control their יצר, judge truthfully, fight the 'battle' of תורה, and come early and stay late in בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות.

phrases.english: "And for strength" — this is one who overpowers his inclination,
"those who turn back battle" —

phrases.aramaic: זֶה שֶׁנּוֹשֵׂא וְנוֹתֵן בְּמִלְחַמְתָּהּ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: this is one who debates back and forth in the battle of Torah,
"at the gate" —
these are those who come early and stay late
in synagogues and study halls.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and completes the explanation of the פסוק begun in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק praises those who overpower their יצר, engage in the battle of תורה, and come early and stay late in בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות.

steps.title: The attribute of justice asks why these people are different
steps.stepSummary: מדת הדין asks the הקב״ה why the people just described get the crown and others do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The attribute of justice said to God: Master of the World, what makes these people different from those?
steps.whatsHappening: The אגדה continues. מדת הדין asks God what makes the people who earn the crown and diadem different from everyone else, and this question sets up God's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 10–11 listed special qualities: ruling over the יצר, judging truthfully, fighting the battle of תורה, and coming early to the בית מדרש. מדת הדין wants to know why only people with these qualities get the reward. The question opens the door for the פסוק God quotes next.

keyTerms.meaning: The attribute of strict justice, pictured here as speaking before God

phrases.english: The attribute of justice said
before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the World,
how are these different from those?
phrases.notes: 'These' are the people from the last few steps who get the crown. 'Those' are everyone else.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרָה מִדַּת הַדִּין לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the qualities listed in Steps 10–11 earn a special reward
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why do the people with these qualities get the crown while others do not?

steps.title: God answers with the verse about those who stumble in judgment
steps.stepSummary: God quotes ישעיהו 28:7: the others reel through wine and 'stumble in judgment.'
steps.simpleTranslation: God answered: 'These also reel through wine and stagger through strong drink... they stumble in judgment.'
steps.whatsHappening: God answers מדת הדין with the very next פסוק in ישעיהו. It describes people who are confused by drink and who stumble when they judge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The others did not earn the crown because they lacked those qualities. Instead they were careless and failed in judgment. The last words, פקו פליליה, are unclear, so the גמרא explains them in the next step.

phrases.english: He said to it:
"These also reel through wine,
and stagger through strong drink [etc.]
phrases.notes: וגו׳ means the פסוק goes on. The גמרא skips ahead to the words it needs.

phrases.english: they stumble in judgment."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהּ: וְגַם אֵלֶּה בַּיַּיִן שָׁגוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of מדת הדין
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The others are like people confused by drink who stumble in judgment, so they do not deserve the crown.

steps.title: Explaining the words פוקה and פלילה
steps.stepSummary: פוקה means גיהנם, and פלילה means judges, each proven from another פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'פוקה' means only גיהנם, as it says: 'This shall not be a stumbling for you.' 'פלילה' means only judges, as it says: 'And he shall pay as the judges determine.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the two hard words, פקו פליליה, from the end of the פסוק God quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פוקה is linked to גיהנם through a פסוק in שמואל. פלילה is linked to judges through a פסוק in שמות. Read together, the phrase means that judges who fail at true judgment stumble into גיהנם. This is the opposite of 'one who judges a true judgment truthfully' from Step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: The place of punishment after death

steps.whatToRemember: The crown goes to those who rule over their יצר and judge truthfully. Those who stumble in judgment end up in גיהנם.

phrases.english: And "puka" means nothing other than Gehenna,
as it says:
"This shall not be a cause of stumbling for you."
And "pelila" means nothing other than judges,
as it says: "And he shall pay as the judges determine."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the hard words in the פסוק quoted in Step 13
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פקו פליליה means that failing judges stumble into גיהנם.

steps.title: משנה: people of a city led astray lose the World to Come
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that the people of an עיר הנדחת have no share in עולם הבא, based on דברים 13:14.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The people of a city that was led into idol worship have no share in עולם הבא, as it says: 'Wicked men went out from among you and led the residents of their city astray.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It adds one more group to the list of those who lose עולם הבא: the people of an עיר הנדחת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה brings the פסוק that describes this case: wicked men lead the people of their own city to serve עבודה זרה. The rest of the משנה will explain exactly when a city counts as an עיר הנדחת.

keyTerms.meaning: A city whose people were led into idol worship
A share in the World to Come

phrases.english: MISHNAH
The people of a city led astray
have no share in the World to Come,
as it says:
"Men, wicked people, went out from your midst,
and led the residents of their city astray, saying."
phrases.notes: דברים 13:14. The פסוק goes on: 'Let us go and serve other gods.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אַנְשֵׁי עִיר הַנִּדַּחַת אֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The people of an עיר הנדחת have no share in עולם הבא.

steps.title: Three conditions for a city to be punished as a whole
steps.stepSummary: A city is only punished as an עיר הנדחת if the people who led it astray are from that city and tribe, a majority was led astray, and the leaders were men.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are not executed as a city unless the people who led it astray are from that city and that tribe, most of the city was led astray, and men did the leading.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists the conditions that must all be met before a city is judged as an עיר הנדחת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three conditions must be met together: the מדיחים must be local (from that city and that שבט), most of the city must be led astray, and the מדיחים must be men. If any one condition is missing, the city is not judged as an עיר הנדחת, as the next step explains. The גמרא later ties some of these conditions to words of the פסוק (Steps 27–28).

keyTerms.meaning: Those who lead others into idol worship

phrases.english: And they are not executed
unless those who led it astray are
from that city and from that tribe,
and unless most of it was led astray,
and unless men led it astray.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines exactly when a city counts as an עיר הנדחת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Local leaders, a majority led astray, and adult men as leaders are all required.

steps.title: When the conditions are missing, they are judged as individuals
steps.stepSummary: If women or children led the city astray, or only a minority strayed, or the leaders were outsiders, each idol worshipper is judged as an individual, with two witnesses and a warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: If women and children led it astray, or only a minority was led astray, or the leaders came from outside, they are like individuals. Each one needs two witnesses and a warning.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה takes the three conditions from Step 16 and explains what happens when one of them is missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the conditions, the special city law does not apply. The people who worshipped idols are still guilty, but each one is handled like any single idol worshipper. That means each needs his own two witnesses and his own warning before he can be punished.

keyTerms.meaning: A warning given before the sin, needed for a בית דין punishment

phrases.english: If women and children led it astray,
or only a minority of it was led astray,
or those who led it astray were from outside it,
these are treated like individuals,
and they need two witnesses and a warning
for each and every one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the result when the conditions of Step 16 are not met
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without the conditions, each idol worshipper is judged as an individual, with two witnesses and a warning.

steps.title: Individuals get a harsher death but keep their property
steps.stepSummary: Individuals are stoned but their property goes to their heirs. A whole city is killed by the sword, and its property is destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here individuals are treated more strictly than the many. Individuals are stoned, so their property is spared. The many are killed by the sword, so their property is destroyed.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה compares the punishment of individual idol worshippers with the punishment of a whole עיר הנדחת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סקילה is a harsher death than סייף, so individuals are punished more strictly in that way. But because their death is harsher, their property goes to their heirs. The city's people get the easier death, so their property is destroyed.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the individual simply has it worse in every way. He gets the harsher death, but he keeps his property for his heirs. The whole city gets the easier death, but loses its property.

phrases.english: This is a stricter point for individuals than for the many:
that individuals are stoned;
therefore their property is spared,
and the many are killed by the sword;
therefore their property is destroyed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts the punishment of individuals (Step 17) with that of a whole city
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Individuals: סקילה, but their property is kept. A whole city: סייף, and its property is destroyed.

steps.title: Traveling caravans can save the city
steps.stepSummary: From the words 'the residents of that city,' the משנה teaches that donkey and camel caravans passing through can save the city.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'You shall surely strike the residents of that city with the sword.' A donkey caravan or camel caravan traveling from place to place saves the city.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה quotes the פסוק about striking the city's residents with the sword. It then teaches that traveling caravans can save the city from this punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of the city's 'residents.' The caravan people were not led astray. If they stayed in the city for a while, they can be counted together with the city's people who did not stray, and then the city might no longer have a majority led astray (Step 16).

keyTerms.meaning: With the edge of the sword

phrases.english: "You shall surely strike the residents of that city
with the edge of the sword."
The donkey caravan and the camel caravan
that travels from place to place,
these save it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכֵּה תַכֶּה אֶת יֹשְׁבֵי הָעִיר הַזֹּאת לְפִי חֶרֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another way a city can escape the עיר הנדחת punishment
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Traveling donkey or camel caravans can save the city.

steps.title: Property of the righteous and the wicked
steps.stepSummary: Based on 'destroy it and all that is in it,' the property of צדיקים inside the city is destroyed, but their property outside is spared. The property of רשעים is destroyed wherever it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Destroy it utterly, and all that is in it and its animals, with the edge of the sword.' From here the Sages said: property of righteous people that is inside the city is destroyed, and property of theirs that is outside is spared. Property of the wicked is destroyed whether it is inside or outside the city.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of rules for an עיר הנדחת. It uses a פסוק to decide which property gets destroyed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'all that is in it' tie the destruction to location. So even innocent people lose whatever property is physically inside the city. The wicked lose everything, because their punishment is personal and does not depend on where the property is.

keyTerms.meaning: Property of the righteous (residents who did not worship idols)
From here they said: a rule learned from the פסוק just quoted

steps.confusionAlert: The צדיקים here are not punished as people. They live. Only their belongings that happen to be inside the city are destroyed together with the city.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״הַחֲרֵם אֹתָהּ וְאֶת כׇּל אֲשֶׁר בָּהּ
phrases.english: As it is stated: 'Destroy it utterly, and all that is in it
and its animals, with the edge of the sword.'
From here they said:
The property of the righteous that is inside it is destroyed,
but what is outside it is spared.
And the property of the wicked,
whether it is inside it or outside it,
these are destroyed.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״הַחֲרֵם אֹתָהּ וְאֶת כׇּל אֲשֶׁר בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's description of the destruction of the city's property introduced in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Property of צדיקים is destroyed only if it is inside the city. Property of רשעים is destroyed wherever it is.

steps.title: Gathering the spoils into the city square
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק requires gathering the spoils into the city's square. If there is no square, one is made. If the square is outside the walls, the city is expanded to bring it inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And you shall gather all its spoils into the midst of its square.' If the city has no square, they make one for it. If its square was outside the city, they bring it inside the city.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה reads the next פסוק very literally. It explains how to fulfill 'into its square' even when the city's layout does not fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'its square,' meaning a square that belongs to and is inside the city. So the city must be adjusted to fit the פסוק: a square is created if none exists, and an outside square is brought inside the city.

keyTerms.meaning: Open public square of a city

phrases.english: As it is stated: 'And all of its spoils
you shall gather into the midst of its square, etc.'
If it has no square,
they make a square for it.
If its square was outside it,
they bring it inside it.
phrases.notes: This means moving the city wall outward so the square ends up inside the city.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר, ״וְאֶת כׇּל שְׁלָלָהּ תִּקְבֹּץ אֶל תּוֹךְ רְחֹבָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next פסוק, which tells how the property is handled before it is burned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The spoils must be gathered into a square inside the city. If needed, a square is created or an outside square is brought inside.

steps.title: Holy items in the city are not burned
steps.stepSummary: 'Its spoils' excludes 'spoils of Heaven.' So הקדש items are redeemed, תרומה is left to rot, and מעשר שני and holy writings are put away in גניזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And you shall burn with fire the city and all its spoils, entirely for ה׳ your God.' 'Its spoils' means the city's own things, not things that belong to Heaven. From here they said: consecrated items in it must be redeemed, תרומות are left to rot, and מעשר שני and holy writings are stored away.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה learns from the word 'its spoils' that holy items in the city are not burned. It then lists what is done with each kind of holy item instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only things that belong to the city's people are burned. Things that belong to Heaven are excluded from the burning. Each holy item is then treated according to its own laws: הקדש is redeemed (and its money goes to the Temple), תרומה is left to decay, and מעשר שני and holy writings are put away respectfully.

keyTerms.meaning: Spoils of Heaven: items belonging to holy causes
Portions of produce given to a כהן
Must be stored away respectfully (put in גניזה)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that even when everything else in the city is destroyed, holy items keep their sanctity and are handled by their own laws.

phrases.english: As it is stated: 'And you shall burn the city with fire,
and all its spoils,
entirely for ה׳ your God.'
'Its spoils,' but not the spoils of Heaven.
phrases.notes: 'Spoils of Heaven' means things that already belong to holy causes, not to the city's people.

phrases.english: From here they said:
The consecrated items in it must be redeemed,
and תרומות must be left to rot,
second tithe and holy writings must be stored away.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וְשָׂרַפְתָּ בָאֵשׁ אֶת הָעִיר וְאֶת כׇּל שְׁלָלָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same פסוק and carves out an exception to the burning of the spoils.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Holy items are excluded from the burning. הקדש is redeemed, תרומה rots, and מעשר שני and holy writings are put in גניזה.

steps.title: Judging the city is like a complete burnt offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון explains 'entirely for ה׳ your God': הקב"ה counts carrying out judgment on an עיר הנדחת as if the people brought an עולה כליל before Him.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the words 'entirely for ה׳ your God,' רבי שמעון said: הקב"ה said, 'If you carry out judgment on the idolatrous city, I will consider it as though you brought a complete burnt offering before Me.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון explains the last words of the פסוק, 'כליל לה׳'. He teaches the spiritual value of carrying out this harsh judgment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word כליל ('entire') is the same word used for an offering that is burned completely on the מזבח. רבי שמעון uses this link to teach that destroying the city is not just a punishment. It counts before הקב"ה like a complete offering.

keyTerms.meaning: Entirely, completely; also the name of an offering that is burned completely
I consider it for you, I credit you

steps.whatToRemember: Carrying out the judgment of an עיר הנדחת properly is valued by הקב"ה like a complete burnt offering.

phrases.english: 'Entirely for ה׳ your God':
Rabbi Shimon said:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:

phrases.aramaic: אִם אַתֶּם עוֹשִׂין דִּין בְּעִיר הַנִּדַּחַת,
phrases.english: If you carry out judgment on the idolatrous city,
I consider it for you

phrases.aramaic: כְּאִילּוּ אַתֶּם מַעֲלִים עוֹלָה כָּלִיל לְפָנַי.
phrases.english: as though you were bringing a complete burnt offering before Me.
phrases.notes: The same word כליל from the פסוק is being read here as the name of a fully burned offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the final words of the same פסוק quoted in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Carrying out judgment on an עיר הנדחת is credited as if one brought an עולה כליל.

steps.title: The ruined city may not even become gardens and orchards
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי learns from 'it shall be a heap forever' that the city may not be turned into gardens or orchards.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And it shall be a heap forever.' It may not be made into gardens and orchards. This is what רבי יוסי הגלילי says.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה reads the פסוק saying the ruined city must stay a heap forever. רבי יוסי הגלילי says that nothing may be done with the land, not even planting gardens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי הגלילי, the word 'heap' means the land must stay a pile of ruins. Any use at all, even farming, is forbidden. This sets up רבי עקיבא's different reading in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A heap forever, a permanent pile of ruins

phrases.english: "And it shall be a heap forever"
it may not be made into gardens and orchards,
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וְהָיְתָה תֵּל עוֹלָם״ – לֹא תֵּעָשֶׂה גַּנּוֹת וּפַרְדֵּסִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's reading of the פסוקים about עיר הנדחת, moving from the burning of the city to what happens to the land afterward.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי הגלילי, the land of an עיר הנדחת may not be used even for gardens and orchards.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: only rebuilding the city is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא reads 'it shall not be built again' to mean the city may not be rebuilt as it was, but it may be made into gardens and orchards.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: 'It shall not be built again' means it may not be built back to how it was. But it may be made into gardens and orchards.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא disagrees with רבי יוסי הגלילי. He says only rebuilding the city as a city is forbidden, so farming the land is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא focuses on the end of the פסוק, 'it shall not be built.' He reads 'built' as 'built as a city again.' Gardens are not buildings, so they are allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: It shall not be built again

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי הגלילי: no use of the land at all, not even gardens. רבי עקיבא: only rebuilding the city is forbidden, and gardens and orchards are allowed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
"It shall not be built again"
phrases.notes: This is the end of the same פסוק, דברים 13:17.

phrases.english: it may not be built back to the way it was,
but it may be made into gardens and orchards.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, the city may not be rebuilt, but its land may be turned into gardens and orchards.

steps.title: When the wicked disappear, anger leaves the world
steps.stepSummary: From 'nothing of the חרם shall cling to your hand,' the משנה teaches that anger stays in the world as long as רשעים are in it, and leaves when they are gone.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And nothing of the חרם shall cling to your hand.' As long as the wicked are in the world, there is anger in the world. Once the wicked are gone from the world, the anger leaves the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a lesson about why the city is destroyed. As long as רשעים are in the world, ה׳'s anger is in the world, and when they are wiped out the anger goes away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק goes on to say 'so that ה׳ will turn from His burning anger.' The משנה ties the two halves together. Removing the wicked city and its spoils is what removes the anger.

keyTerms.meaning: Something set aside for destruction, here the spoils of the city

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה closes the topic of עיר הנדחת with a message: wiping out the wicked removes Divine anger from the world.

phrases.english: "And nothing of the devoted property shall cling to your hand"
for as long as the wicked are in the world,
there is burning anger in the world;
once the wicked are gone from the world,
the burning anger leaves the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next פסוק and closes the משנה with an aggadic lesson.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Divine anger stays in the world as long as רשעים exist, and leaves when they are destroyed.

steps.title: The leaders must act themselves, be at least two, and be grown men
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא. 'They went out' means the leaders themselves and not agents. 'Men' means at least two, or, by another reading, not women and not children.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'They went out' means they themselves, not agents. 'Men' means no fewer than two. Another explanation: 'men' and not women, 'men' and not children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a ברייתא that reads the פסוק about the people who led the city astray, one word at a time. These words set the conditions for who counts as a מדיח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'They went out' requires the מדיחים to act in person, so sending agents does not count. 'Men' in the plural means at least two people. The second reading uses the same word to leave out women and children.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
phrases.notes: Here the גמרא starts working on the פסוק in דברים 13:14.

phrases.english: "They went out": they themselves, and not agents.
"Men": "men" means no fewer than two.
Another explanation: "men" and not women,
"men" and not children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The משנה has ended, and the גמרא opens by reading the פסוק that defines the מדיחים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מדיחים must lead the city astray in person, must be at least two, and must be grown men.

steps.title: More conditions from the פסוק: not a border city, same city, and warning for each person
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. 'בני בליעל' means people who threw off the yoke of Heaven. 'From your midst' excludes a border city. 'The inhabitants of their city' excludes people of another city. 'Saying' teaches that every person needs עדים and התראה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'בני בליעל' means sons who threw off the yoke of Heaven from their necks. 'From your midst' means not a border city. 'The inhabitants of their city' means not the inhabitants of another city. 'Saying' teaches that there must be witnesses and a warning for each and every person.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going through the פסוק word by word. Each word adds another condition for a city to become an עיר הנדחת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בני בליעל' is read as 'בלי עול', meaning without a yoke. 'From your midst' limits the law to cities inside the land, so a city on the border is not included. 'Saying' teaches that each person needs his own עדים and התראה.

keyTerms.meaning: Worthless people, read here as 'without a yoke'
A warning given before the sin, needed for punishment

steps.confusionAlert: 'Saying' does not mean the מדיחים must speak in some special way. The ברייתא uses this word to teach that every single person needs his own witnesses and warning.

phrases.english: "Benei veliyya'al":
sons who threw off the yoke of Heaven from their necks.
phrases.notes: This is a play on the word בליעל, read as בלי עול, without a yoke.

phrases.english: "From your midst": and not from the border.
"The inhabitants of their city": and not the inhabitants of another city.
"Saying": that witnesses are needed
and a warning for each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״בְּנֵי בְּלִיַּעַל״ – בָּנִים שֶׁפָּרְקוּ עוֹל שָׁמַיִם מִצַּוְּארֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, reading the rest of the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A border city cannot become an עיר הנדחת, the people led astray must be from that city, and every person needs עדים and התראה.
steps.whyThisMatters: The condition 'the inhabitants of their city' leads into the next discussion, about whether the מדיחים must also be from the same שבט.

steps.title: Can one city be split between two tribes?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says one city can be divided between two שבטים. ריש לקיש says it cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רבי יוחנן says one city can be divided between two tribes. ריש לקיש says one city cannot be divided between two tribes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a מחלוקת between אמוראים. They argue whether a single city can sit partly in one שבט's land and partly in another's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a city can be split, it is possible for someone to live in the city but belong to a different שבט. If it cannot be split, everyone in the city belongs to the same שבט. This sets up the challenge in the next step, which uses the משנה's wording about 'that city and that tribe.'

phrases.english: It was stated: Rabbi Yochanan says:
one city can be divided between two tribes;
and Reish Lakish says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין חוֹלְקִין עִיר אַחַת לִשְׁנֵי שְׁבָטִים.
phrases.english: one city cannot be divided between two tribes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר, רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: חוֹלְקִין עִיר אַחַת לִשְׁנֵי שְׁבָטִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic, connected to the משנה's rule that the מדיחים must be from that city and that שבט.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן says a city can be split between two שבטים. ריש לקיש says it cannot.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן points to the משנה, which requires the מדיחים to be 'from that city and from that tribe.' This suggests someone could be from the city but not from the שבט, which means a city can be split.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן challenged ריש לקיש from the משנה: 'Unless its מדיחים are from that city and from that tribe.' Doesn't this mean that even if the מדיחים are from that city, if they are also from that tribe then yes, and if not then no? Learn from this that one city can be divided between two tribes!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן attacks ריש לקיש's view using the wording of the משנה. If the משנה needs to say both 'that city' and 'that tribe,' a person could be from the city and still not be from the tribe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every city belonged entirely to one שבט, saying 'that tribe' would add nothing, since anyone from the city would already be from the שבט. The extra words only make sense if a city can be split between two שבטים, which is רבי יוחנן's view. So the משנה seems to go against ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: Its מדיחים, the people who led it astray
Is it not that…?, a way of pushing a reading of a source

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan raised an objection to Reish Lakish:

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּהוּ מַדִּיחֶיהָ מֵאוֹתָהּ הָעִיר וּמֵאוֹתוֹ שֵׁבֶט –
phrases.english: "Unless its subverters are from that city and from that tribe"

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו, אַף עַל גַּב דְּמַדִּיחֶיהָ מֵאוֹתָהּ הָעִיר,
phrases.english: Is it not that even though its subverters are from that city,
if they are from that tribe, yes,
and if not, no?
phrases.notes: Meaning: if they are not from the same שבט, the city does not become an עיר הנדחת.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: חוֹלְקִין עִיר אַחַת לִשְׁנֵי שְׁבָטִים!
phrases.english: Learn from this: one city can be divided between two tribes!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's side of the מחלוקת from step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that one city cannot be divided between two שבטים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה requires the מדיחים to be from 'that city and that tribe.' Mentioning the שבט separately is only needed if a person can live in a city without belonging to its שבט, and that is only possible if a city can be split.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common way the גמרא argues: if a source uses words that seem extra, they must be teaching something, and that can decide a מחלוקת.

steps.title: The person may simply own property in a city of another tribe
steps.stepSummary: The proof from the משנה is rejected. A man can be from the city but not from its שבט if he inherited property there or received it as a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is a case where the property fell to him as an inheritance. Or, it is a case where they gave it to him as a gift.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא, defending ריש לקיש, pushes away רבי יוחנן's proof from the משנה. It shows another way someone could be 'from the city but not from the שבט.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן assumed that only a split city could have residents from another שבט. The גמרא says no: a man from one שבט can own property in another שבט's city through ירושה (for example, from his mother's family) or through a gift. So the משנה's wording does not prove that cities were divided.

keyTerms.meaning: No; this introduces a rejection of the proof

phrases.english: No, it is where it fell to him as an inheritance.
phrases.notes: 'It' is property in that city. He could inherit it from his mother's side, who came from a different שבט.

phrases.english: Alternatively, where they gave it to him as a gift.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by rejecting the inference drawn from the משנה in step 30.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה's wording, not רבי יוחנן's position itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed that living in a city means belonging to its שבט's land. A person can own property in another שבט's city through inheritance or a gift.

steps.title: Nine cities from two tribes suggests a split city
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש from a פסוק: nine cities came from two שבטים, which sounds like four and a half from each. That would mean one city was split.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: 'Nine cities from these two tribes.' Doesn't this mean four and a half from this tribe and four and a half from that tribe? Conclude from it that one city can be divided between two tribes!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן brings a new challenge against ריש לקיש, this time from a פסוק in יהושע about cities given to the לויים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says nine cities came from two שבטים together. If each שבט gave an equal share, each gave four and a half cities. Half a city from each side means one city was shared between two שבטים, which goes against ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not that...? (introduces the reading being pushed)
Learn from it; conclude from it

phrases.english: He raised an objection against him: "Nine cities
from these two tribes."
Is it not four and a half from this one,
and four and a half from that one?
And learn from it: we divide one city
between two tribes!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: עָרִים תֵּשַׁע מֵאֵת שְׁנֵי הַשְּׁבָטִים הָאֵלֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from the משנה was rejected, רבי יוחנן brings a new proof from a פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that one city cannot be divided between two שבטים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nine cities from two שבטים, divided equally, gives four and a half each. So one city must have been shared between them.

steps.title: It could be four from one tribe and five from the other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The nine cities need not be split evenly. One שבט could have given four and the other five.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Four from this tribe and five from that tribe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends ריש לקיש by reading the פסוק differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof only works if both שבטים gave equal amounts. The גמרא says the split could be uneven, four and five. Then every city stays whole and no city is shared.

phrases.english: No, four from this one
and five from that one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by rejecting the equal-split reading proposed in step 32.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the assumption that the nine cities were divided equally.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Nothing in the פסוק requires an even split. An uneven split of four and five keeps every city whole.

steps.title: Then the verse should say which tribe gave more
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the four-and-five answer. If the split was uneven, the פסוק should have spelled out which שבט gave the extra city.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let it state it explicitly!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. This sets up the next move, which comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grouping the nine cities together without saying who gave what makes the most sense if the shares were equal. If one שבט gave five and the other four, we would expect the פסוק to say so clearly. So the four-and-five answer now looks weak.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it state it explicitly; let it spell it out

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא answers this question on the next amud, so don't treat the four-and-five answer as either rejected or final yet.

phrases.english: If so, let it state it explicitly!
phrases.notes: He means the פסוק should tell us which שבט gave five and which gave four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the four-and-five answer given in step 33.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the nine cities were split four and five.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the shares were unequal, the פסוק would have said which שבט gave more. Its silence suggests the shares were equal.
